To test sensitivity to contamination severity, we evaluate at $\rho = 0.6$ (seed\,42 only).

ESS-only (PPL 17.770) falls within 0.004 of uniform (17.766); its small PPL increase reflects its low baseline effectiveness at $\rho{=}0.4$ rather than contamination resilience---a method that provides no benefit cannot lose much when conditions worsen.
With more synthetic samples per batch, the ESS floor binds earlier, preventing the solver from raising $b$ enough to suppress them effectively.

These are single-seed results and should be interpreted accordingly.

Detect \& Remove achieves the lowest PPL (17.290), outperforming all reweighting methods by ${\geq}0.35$.

Over 25{,}991 training micro-batches (seed\,42), only ${\sim}2\%$ are sufficiently real-dominated ($\aeff(0) \geq \tau$) to require no reweighting.
The method is active on nearly every batch.

The per-batch $\bstar$ distribution (mean 1.43, median 0.87, std 1.93, range $[0, 20]$) adapts continuously to each batch's contamination composition without any held-out signal.
